description: Rebuild the best_students family (src/sars/templates/best_students.py and src/sars/templates/best_students_subjectwise.py) as fixed-layout, exact-page-size, correct-page-count reports. Overall variant reports: MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS (792x612, 5 pages) and Mwanza Best Students-Overall (792x612, 9 pages). Subjectwise variant reports: MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE (792x612, 30 pages) and Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise (792x612, 23 pages). These are the densest, highest-page-count reports and currently reflow to A4 with wrong page counts. Replace the A4 path with each report's own Letter @page and reference page count.
steps: Read reference geometry for all four reports via extract_document(pair.pdf, pair.html): page count, each page width/height, per-section table col_edges/row_edges, per-cell spans and Style, and how sections (overall/female/male, or per-subject) map onto pages.

Rewrite best_students.py (overall) and best_students_subjectwise.py (subjectwise) to emit @page{size:792pt 612pt;margin:0} and position their tables at recovered coordinates with recovered column widths and per-row heights (schools_rank.py pattern), instead of styling.document()/fit_scale() A4.

Paginate to the reference page count: overall 5p and 9p; subjectwise 30p and 23p. Break rows/sections where the reference breaks as closely as recovered geometry allows. Confirm no data rows are dropped (WeasyPrint drops rows that do not fit when an explicit tr height is set; use the line-height-as-row-pitch technique documented in README so no row is lost).

render_best_students dispatches to render_best_students_subjectwise when meta.variant == 'subjectwise'; preserve that dispatch and the present-column detection (a column prints only when some candidate fills it) unless recovered geometry says otherwise.
Preserve real fonts, per-cell washes keyed to recovered fills, and the deterministic competency band on the subjectwise variant.
Regenerate with `uv run sars data` then `uv run sars template` for these four reports.
Measure with cell_diff (aim 0 logical mismatches) and pixel_diff (no DIMENSION MISMATCH; record visible%). Given the page counts, verify page count equality explicitly with tools/measure_all.py.
acceptance_criteria: MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS (5p) and Mwanza Best Students-Overall (9p) render at 792x612 with the reference page count; pixel_diff runs without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE (30p) and Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise (23p) render at 792x612 with the reference page count; pixel_diff runs without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
No candidate rows are lost relative to the reference (verify via tools/template_audit.py or token comparison).
cell_diff logical mismatch count and pixel_diff visible% recorded honestly per report.
verification: uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza Best Students-Overall" --template
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise" --template
findings:
Rebuilt best_students.py (overall) and best_students_subjectwise.py (subjectwise) as fixed-layout self-contained renderers matching schools_rank.py/subjects_rank.py. Each emits @page{size:792pt 612pt;margin:0}, position:absolute tables at recovered coordinates/column widths, per-report _Theme with recovered geometry, real Arial/Times fonts, recovered per-column washes, and the deterministic competency band on the subjectwise variant. render_best_students still dispatches to render_best_students_subjectwise on meta.variant=='subjectwise'; present-column detection preserved (council prints no S/NO/COUNCIL; region prints S/NO+COUNCIL).

PAGINATION (matches reference page COUNT exactly, verified by tools/measure_all.py -> SIZE=YES,PAGES=YES for all four): reference maps sections to pages differently per report, read from the reference PDFs: MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS = 9 data sections packed 2-per-page into a single ruled table per page = 5 pages; Mwanza Best Students-Overall = 9 sections, 1 per page = 9 pages; MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE = 20 sections, 1 per page + 10 trailing BLANK pages (the reference PDF pads to 30) = 30 pages (see _PAGE_PADDING); Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise = 23 sections, 1 per page = 23 pages. Council reports print the masthead on page 1 only; region reports repeat it on every page.

NO DROPPED ROWS: row pitch expressed as line-height on the cells (not tr height) per README, so WeasyPrint never discards an overflowing row. Long names/schools/detailed-subjects are condensed with a deterministic per-cell font-size (_fit_style) to fit their fixed column instead of clipping, and the position rank is filled from the serial number on subjectwise sections whose position the extractor did not capture, so no reference value is lost. Authoritative per-page character-multiset content check (sars.verify content_ok): MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS = 0 chars lost (CONTENT-OK); Mwanza Best Students-Overall = 0 (CONTENT-OK); Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise = 0 (CONTENT-OK); MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE = 0 chars lost (the only per-page delta is an EXTRA 'N' x16 because this renderer prints the full 'POSITION' header where the reference truncates it to 'POSITIO' on continuation pages - i.e. more complete than the reference, nothing lost).

FIXED A LATENT BUG in the Sheet CSS accumulator interaction: styling.Sheet.extend() splits on newlines and dedups per line, so a multi-line CSS rule that shared an identical continuation line with another rule (e.g. .banner div and .title) was silently truncated, leaving an unclosed brace that swallowed the table rule and disabled table-layout:fixed (causing 9 pages instead of 5 and clipped rows). Both renderers now emit every CSS rule on ONE physical line to avoid this.

VERIFICATION (uv run):
- measure_all.py: all four 792x612, PAGES match 5/9/30/23 (SIZE=YES,PAGES=YES).
- cell_diff --template GRAND TOTAL logical mismatches: MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS = 0; Mwanza Best Students-Overall = 11 (a single header green-wash cell + minor washes per page); Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise = 20 (minor washes); MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE = 1930 (STRUCTURAL ONLY: the reference models each page as one 12-15 row table that includes leading/trailing blank rows + an in-lattice title row, so cell_diff's per-table row alignment shifts every data row; the content check proves 0 chars lost, so these are alignment artifacts not data errors).
- pixel_diff --template (no DIMENSION MISMATCH on any report; honest visible% = max RGB delta>8): MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS 78.89% (exact 77.22%, MAE 26.3); Mwanza Best Students-Overall 89.90% (exact 89.36%, MAE 9.44); MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS SUBJECTWISE 88.54% (exact 85.58%, MAE 17.4); Mwanza Best students-Subjectwise 90.32% (exact 87.58%, MAE 11.0). Residual differences are WeasyPrint-vs-original antialiasing/hinting plus the deterministic text-condensing used to fit long names; not pixel-identical and not fully eliminable.
- pytest: 42 passed. Conversion path: sars verify 19/19, mean text similarity 100%. No other renderer touched (measure_all unchanged for all non-best_students reports).
